svg.title: Transverse section of a dicotyledonous stem
svg.desc: A plan diagram of a dicot stem with epidermis, collenchyma, cortex, a ring of vascular bundles each with a sclerenchyma cap, phloem, cambium and xylem, medullary rays and pith, beside a magnified vascular bundle showing the cells.
svg.text: Left: plan diagram (tissues only). Right: one vascular bundle magnified, showing cells.

g.data-info: One layer of cells covered by a waxy cuticle; protects the stem and reduces water loss.
Living cells with walls thickened at the corners, just under the epidermis; flexible support for the young stem.
Parenchyma (packing) tissue between the epidermis and the vascular bundles; stores food (starch) and gives support when turgid.
Parenchyma between the vascular bundles, linking the pith and cortex.
Fibres with very thick lignified walls on the outer side of each bundle; strengthen the stem against bending.
Sieve tubes and companion cells on the outer side of the bundle; translocate sucrose and amino acids in either direction.
On the inner side of the bundle; vessels with lignified walls carry water and mineral ions upwards and support the stem.
A thin layer of dividing (meristem) cells between xylem and phloem; produces new xylem inwards and new phloem outwards.
Parenchyma (packing) tissue between the epidermis and the vascular bundles; stores food (starch) and gives support when turgid.
Fibres with very thick lignified walls on the outer side of each bundle; strengthen the stem against bending.
Sieve tubes and companion cells on the outer side of the bundle; translocate sucrose and amino acids in either direction.
Wide, thin-walled phloem cell with little cytoplasm and no nucleus; joined end to end through sieve plates.
Small cell with dense cytoplasm, a nucleus and many mitochondria beside each sieve tube element; loads sucrose by active transport.
A thin layer of dividing (meristem) cells between xylem and phloem; produces new xylem inwards and new phloem outwards.
Living packing cells between the xylem vessels.
Large vessel formed later, nearer the cambium: wide lumen, thick lignified walls with pits.
Small vessel formed first, nearest the pith; its lignin is in rings or spirals so it can stretch as the stem grows.
